output.summary: KEP-3130 proposed adding a kube-apiserver-generated transaction UID to the kms-plugin envelope interface so that kube-apiserver, kms-plugin and KMS calls for one envelope operation can be correlated in logs. The KEP is now replaced by KEP-3299 KMS v2 Improvements, which carried the work forward.
output.rationale: Correlating a kube-apiserver->kms-plugin->KMS envelope operation today relies on approximate timestamps, which the readme calls unreliable. The KEP chose a generated UID over reusing the audit ID, because audit IDs can be set by users, are shared across requests, are absent for cached DEK operations, and do not cover every KMS call. The status history and kep.yaml record the replacement by KEP-3299 from 2022-06-17, and later discussion on the KEP-3302 PR (the KMS v2 work) shows UID handling moved into that design.
output.outcome_reason:
The sources do not give a detailed reason for the replacement. They record only that KEP-3130 "is replaced by KEP-3299 KMS v2 Improvements" and that the KEP "has been replaced" by the KMS v2 Improvements KEP. The KMS v2 design was being reviewed in PR #3302 at the time, and the UID was kept as part of that proto. Those sources do not explicitly state why the replacement happened.</outcome_reason>

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes extending the signature of the kms-plugin interface to include the transaction ID (to be generated by the kube-apiserver), which kms-plugin could pass to KMS.
AuditID can be configured by the user with the `Audit-ID` header in the API server request. Multiple requests can be sent to the kube-apiserver with the same Audit-ID.
The API server caches DEKs and for the DEK that's available in the cache, the kube-apiserver will not generate an envelope operation.
This KEP has been replaced by https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/3299-kms-v2-improvements
We decided to keep UID as part of the proto since it is a core change we are introducing in v2 and it's not optional.
